# Publish gate report

**Going out:** Creator post (paid), UK audience, Pebblebrook Tea Co.

## Checks

**1. Claims:** "packed by hand in Bristol" is on the policy list (every tin is packed by hand in Bristol). Assam as a product is a product fact, fine as written. No other claims. Pass.

**2. Regulated claims:** No health, money, legal, environmental, children or price content. "Ten minutes away from my phone" is a lifestyle statement, not a wellbeing claim. Pass.

**3. House style:** Short, specific and natural. No banned phrases or AI tells (no stock openers, no slogan closer). The policy gives no voice rules beyond this, so I can't score against reference writing. Pass.

**4. Disclosure:** **Fail.** The channel is a paid creator post, and the draft has no label at all. In the UK, paid partnerships must be clearly labelled upfront (ASA/CAP rules), before the reader engages. The label needs to be at the start, in plain words, not buried in hashtags or at the end.

## Fixed
- Added an upfront label (suggested text below).

**Suggested version:**
> **Ad | Paid partnership with Pebblebrook Tea Co.**
> My afternoon reset is a pot of Pebblebrook's Assam and ten minutes away from my phone. Their tins are packed by hand in Bristol, which I love.

Also use the platform's own paid-partnership / branded-content tool, if it has one.

## Needs a decision
- Confirm the exact label wording the team wants (policy doesn't specify; "Ad" or "Paid partnership" are the safe choices). Suggested answer: "Ad | Paid partnership".
- If the creator also received free product or commission, say so in the label or brief.

## Approver
The policy names no approver, so the approval needs to come from you (the user). I haven't recorded any approval, and this version needs an explicit yes to the exact final text, with the label, before it goes out. As it stands, the original draft should not be published.

```json
{"issues": [{"quote": "My afternoon reset is a pot of Pebblebrook's Assam", "type": "missing_disclosure"}], "publish": false}
```
